claims.text: A tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy can serve as an effective low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
Minimizing elements that form long-lived radioactive isotopes limits the alloy's activation under fusion conditions.
The proposed tungsten-based HEA has a high melting point.
The proposed tungsten-based HEA has excellent mechanical strength at elevated temperatures.
The proposed tungsten-based HEA is resistant to irradiation damage.
The alloy's high melting point, elevated-temperature strength, and irradiation resistance limit degradation under fusion conditions.
Tungsten combined with refractory elements such as tantalum, vanadium, and chromium can be formulated to minimize activation concerns.
The proposed alloy will maintain a stable, finely dispersed multiphase microstructure during fusion-relevant exposure.
A stable, finely dispersed multiphase microstructure resists radiation-induced defect accumulation.
A stable, finely dispersed multiphase microstructure mitigates crack propagation.
The selected combination of refractory elements raises the alloy's melting point.
The selected combination of refractory elements enhances the alloy's mechanical robustness.
The selected combination of refractory elements enhances the alloy's irradiation resistance.
Excluding or minimizing elements prone to producing long-lived radioactive isotopes allows the alloy to maintain low activation.
The tungsten-based HEA will retain its mechanical properties during high-temperature plasma exposure better than pure tungsten or reduced-activation ferritic-martensitic steels.
The tungsten-based HEA will exhibit less radiation-induced activation than pure tungsten or reduced-activation ferritic-martensitic steels.
The tungsten-based HEA will have better structural integrity under fusion-reactor operating conditions than the stated baseline materials.
The proposed benefits depend on maintaining a homogeneous microstructure and precise compositional control.
Phase segregation can diminish the alloy's low-activation and high-temperature performance.
Uncontrolled impurity inclusion can diminish the alloy's low-activation and high-temperature performance.
